items.title: Corridor wait complaint escalated to clinical negligence claim
items.description: A 12-hour A&E corridor wait complaint was initially graded low priority. Delayed investigation meant the patient's condition worsened. The complaint escalated to a clinical negligence claim with significant liability.
items.recommendation: Always check for clinical deterioration during extended waits. Prioritize corridor wait complaints involving elderly or vulnerable patients.

items.title: Missing medical records delayed investigation by 6 weeks
items.description: Investigation of a surgical complaint was delayed because medical records from a referring hospital were not requested until week 3. The 25-day target was missed.
items.recommendation: Request all relevant records from referring/receiving hospitals at case opening, not during investigation.

items.title: Duty of candour not triggered despite moderate harm
items.description: An investigation concluded moderate harm occurred but duty of candour was not formally triggered because the harm classification was disputed between teams.
items.recommendation: When harm level is disputed, default to the higher classification and trigger duty of candour. Document the assessment.

items.title: Similar maternity complaints revealed systemic staffing issue
items.description: Three maternity complaints over 6 months all cited inadequate midwife-to-patient ratios during night shifts. Individual investigations missed the pattern.
items.recommendation: Run similar case matching for all maternity complaints to identify staffing and systemic patterns early.

items.title: Unsigned investigation report invalidated the response
items.description: A complaint response was sent before the investigating clinician signed off the report. The complainant's solicitor challenged the validity of the response.
items.recommendation: Verify all investigation reports are signed by the investigating clinician and approved before sending responses.
